quote.text: In order to improve your game, you must first study the endgame.
quote.author: — José Raúl Capablanca

method.title: Understand, announce,
method.body: Every position plays out in two steps, identical across every mode. That's what turns a vague idea into a reflex.
method.step1Body: Every theme opens with a 5-to-8-screen lesson: the key idea, typical positions, arrows and highlighted squares, one mini-exercise per screen.
method.step2Body: Win, draw, or loss? Before touching a piece, you evaluate the position. A correct announcement earns points; a wrong one comes back sooner.
method.step3Body: The judge defends with the best move. A losing move is undone and the correct moves are shown. You continue until promotion, mate, or a held draw.
method.boardHeading: Spot the right move at a glance
method.boardBody: Every exercise starts from a real tablebase position. The White King must escort the pawn: Kd7 cuts off the Black King.

tempo.title: Winning isn't enough. Win
tempo.body: On attack, it counts the moves to the queen or mate. Every wasted tempo adds a red box and the most direct move is shown to you. On defense, it counts the moves held.

about.title: Endgames
about.body: ZugChess was born from the belief that chess endgames — often seen as dry and technical — can be learned with method, efficiency, and even enjoyment. You don't have to be a grandmaster to understand king and pawn versus king.
about.card1Body: Every move is evaluated by a tablebase or a grandmaster-strength engine. No approximation, no vaguely good moves — the exact truth, always.
about.card2Body: The FSRS algorithm calculates the optimal moment to review each position, just before forgetting sets in. Five minutes a day is enough.
about.card3Body: Understand the plan, announce the result, prove it on the board. Three identical steps for every position — that's what builds the reflex.
about.closingBody: ZugChess is developed by chess enthusiasts who are tired of overcomplicated apps. Every design decision starts from one question: does this actually help you improve?
